pure-announcement.rationale: It is Bush's 1945 Atlantic essay proposing the memex and associative trails, not a product launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: Nothing in the nearest concepts (evals, proxy capture, code graphs, context layer) covers associative trails, the memex, or the selection-over-storage bottleneck.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The essay is itself the primary source, and its design arguments (indexing is artificial, selection is the bottleneck) are checkable against eighty years of hypertext and knowledge-tool history.

durability.rationale: The core claims — consultation, not storage, is the bottleneck of the record; selection should work by association rather than hierarchical indexing; trails between items are durable, shareable artifacts — have stayed true and generative for eighty years even though the microfilm-era gadgetry around them is long superseded.

actionability.rationale: The trail mechanism is specified concretely enough to build from (named trails, joining two items with persistent mutual codes, side trails, sharing a trail into another person's store) and is the direct design principle behind hypertext and modern linked knowledge bases.

atomicity.rationale: The durable memex-and-trails core is bundled with several separable period excursions — walnut head cameras and dry photography, the Vocoder speech typewriter, arithmetic and logic machines, and neural-interface speculation — so the note carries multiple ideas and the split is the finding.
